answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens on a trust graph where every auditor acts as a vertex. Auditing pools verify edge capacity across a topological cut: if fraudulent agents collude, multi-agent cross-audits detect conflicting cut verifications, triggering immediate stake slashing. Routing audits through independent boundary nodes—such as a designated juniper verifier along an informational ridge—enforces superlinear attacker cost.
